name: Corner lip lift

card.summary: Surgical skin excision at the corners of the mouth to raise downturned commissures; evidence is surgeon case experience, and visible scarring is a recognised risk.
card.aka: Corner of the mouth lift, commissure lift, smile lift
card.note: Scarring at the mouth corner, asymmetry and under-correction are documented risks; published evidence is mostly surgeon series.

quick.overview:
A corner lip lift is a surgical procedure in which a small piece of skin is removed at or just above the corner of the mouth so that downturned corners sit higher. It is sometimes called a smile lift. It is often performed together with an upper lip lift, and some surgeons describe it as a way to widen the visible lip.

On looksmax.org, users discuss it as a way to change mouth proportions and make lips look fuller or the smile more prominent. Published literature consists mainly of surgeon-authored descriptions and case series; no controlled trials were found.
quick.mechanism: Skin is excised in a lens or triangle shape above the oral commissure and the wound is closed, which pulls the corner upward. Some variants also involve the muscles around the mouth. Reports describe the result as a change of a few millimetres.
quick.risks: Reported risks include visible scarring, hypertrophic scarring, asymmetry, under-correction, stiffness, numbness and distortion of the smile. A surgeon-authored review states that lip lift design is more complex than most practitioners realize. Some posters on looksmax.org say surgeons advised against the procedure for aesthetic reasons.

lead: A corner lip lift (also called a corner of the mouth lift, commissure lift or smile lift) is a surgical procedure that raises the corners of the mouth, typically by removing a small lens-shaped piece of skin at or just above the oral commissure [1][2]. People who choose it are usually those whose mouth corners turn downward at rest, giving a neutral or sad-looking expression, and who want the resting mouth to read as more upturned and the smile to look more prominent [1][2].

Because the mouth corners move upward, some patients and surgeons also describe the result as a change in the apparent shape of the lips, with the visible lip looking wider or slightly fuller. In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed in terms of mouth width, lip fullness and lower-third proportions, usually alongside upper lip lifts and jaw or chin work [3][4][5].

The procedure is described in the plastic surgery literature as one of four broad lip-lifting approaches, and it is frequently combined with an upper lip lift [1][2]. Published material consists mostly of surgeon-authored technique descriptions and case series; a 2022 article in the Aesthetic Surgery Journal reports more than 2,440 consecutive lip lifts and discusses when to add a corner lift to a deep-plane upper lip lift [2]. Surgeons report high patient satisfaction with lip lifts in general, though no single technique has become the standard [1].

paras: Wikipedia's lip lift article, summarising a 2014 systematic review, sorts surgical lip lifts into four categories: direct (gull-wing) lifts, indirect lifts, corner-of-the-mouth lifts and V-Y advancement. The corner procedure targets the commissures, in one variant by excising a lens-shaped (lenticular) area of skin above the upper oral commissure; it is also known as the smile lift [1].

Lip lifts as a group developed from the 1980s, when surgeons looked for lasting alternatives to injectable collagen for thin or ageing lips. Early papers on surgical lip lifting appeared in the mid-1980s, and later reports covered direct excision techniques and vermilion advancement [1].

Indirect lifts, such as the subnasal 'bullhorn' lift, remove tissue under the nose to expose more upper lip and are often paired with a corner lift [1]. The surgeons behind the CUPID technique describe the corner lift as a design element to be added when appropriate, to keep the upper lip balanced and maintain exposure of the lateral vermilion [2].

Cosmetically, the procedure is chosen to change how the mouth looks at rest and when smiling. Surgeons describe candidates as people whose corners sit low or turn down, and the corner lift is sometimes added to an upper lip lift so that the lip and the corners are treated together [1][2].

On looksmax.org, members discuss it as a way to adjust mouth width and the proportion between mouth and chin or jaw. One member describes it as a first step to set new proportions ahead of a planned custom jaw and chin implant [3]. Another thread suggests it can be an alternative or addition to fillers for people with small or concave-down lips [5].

No controlled trials of corner lip lift were found. Published material consists of a 2022 surgeon-authored technique paper covering more than 2,440 consecutive lip lifts, graded by its authors as level 4 evidence, which focuses on upper lip design and the decision to add a corner lift [2]. A 2014 systematic review of non-filling lip augmentation methods, summarised on Wikipedia, found that philtrum length decreases with indirect lip lifts but not with V-Y advancement [1].

Wikipedia's lip lift article lists numbness, stiffness, pain, paresthesia, lip distortion or lengthening, smile deformation, speech impediment, asymmetry, under-correction and visible or hypertrophic scarring among reported complications of lip lifts generally. It singles out skin removal at or directly above the white roll as linked to unfavourable scarring and stiffness, and notes that patients typically need about a week of rest [1].

Scar visibility at the mouth corner is the concern most often raised in forum discussion; one member asking for after photographs said scars were their only worry because they could not find examples [5].

A looksmax.org member who posted about their corner lip lift wrote that several surgeons had advised against it in order to preserve white lip length, but that they were pleased with the result and planned it as a proportion change before a custom jaw and chin implant [3]. Another thread shares a video describing the procedure and claims it widens the mouth by a couple of millimetres; a reply questions whether a wider mouth suits a narrow maxilla [4]. A third thread asks for after pictures and discusses whether a corner lift would make small lips look fuller compared with fillers [5].

timeline.event: Fanous publishes on correcting thin lips with a lip lift, among the early surgical lip-lift reports cited by Wikipedia [1].
Austin publishes on the lip lift [1].
Greenwald publishes on the lip lift [1].
Weston and colleagues report 28 years of experience with direct excision lip lifts [1].
A systematic review groups non-filling lip augmentation into four categories, including corner-of-the-mouth lift [1].
The CUPID deep plane upper lip lift and simplified corner lift is described in Aesthetic Surgery Journal, based on more than 2,440 consecutive lip lifts [2].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org the corner lip lift is discussed as a way to widen the mouth, add apparent lip size and adjust lower-third proportions, usually alongside other surgery [3][4].

claims.claim: A corner lip lift makes the mouth wider and lips look fuller.
claims.believers: A forum poster summarising a video says the procedure restructures muscles around the mouth and results in a wider mouth by a few millimetres [4].
claims.experts: No controlled study measuring mouth width after corner lip lift was found; the surgeon literature focuses on upper lip balance and vermilion exposure [2].

claims.claim: The procedure can be used to set new facial proportions before other surgery such as jaw or chin implants.
claims.believers: One member reports having it done first to establish new proportions before a planned custom jaw and chin implant, despite surgeons advising against it [3].
claims.experts: Surgeon-authored work describes lip lift design in terms of lip balance and facial harmony, but no study of sequencing with skeletal procedures was found [2].

claims.claim: Surgeons advise against the corner lift to protect white lip length, but some patients choose it anyway.
claims.believers: A member who had the procedure says several surgeons advised against it to preserve white lip length, yet they are satisfied with the result [3].
claims.experts: Wikipedia lists visible or hypertrophic scarring, lip distortion and smile deformation among documented complications of lip lifts [1]; no comparative study of patient satisfaction after corner lifts was found.

claims.claim: A corner lip lift can stand in for or complement fillers in small lips.
claims.believers: A thread poster says a corner lift would make small lips look fuller and bring out the smile, and prefers it to filler [5].
claims.experts: Surgeon literature on lip lifts concerns lip balance and vermilion exposure; no study comparing corner lifts with fillers was found [1][2].

angle.text: A corner lip lift changes the resting angle of the mouth by raising the commissures a few millimetres. Patients use it to soften a downturned or tired-looking mouth and, as forum users describe it, to make the lips appear wider or fuller in proportion to the rest of the face [1][4].
